I can’t keep checking that page every hour from this chat — I have no background/automation capability here. I can, however, help you set up monitoring you can run yourself (or via a service) and show exactly how to get notified when the wording changes.

Options — pick one and I’ll give the exact steps/files you need:

1) No-code web-monitoring services (fastest)
- Visualping, Distill Web Monitor (browser extension/cloud), ChangeTower, Wachete, or PageCrawl.  
- Pros: easy to set up, email/SMS/Slack notifications, visual diffs.  
- Cons: may be paid for frequent checks or advanced rules.

If you want this route, tell me which service you prefer and your notification channel (email/Slack/SMS), and I’ll write step-by-step setup instructions.

2) Browser extension (client-side)
- Use Distill Web Monitor or Visualping extension to check hourly and notify you locally or via their cloud account.
- Good if you only need monitoring on a single workstation.

3) Lightweight script + cron (self-hosted)
- You run a small script on a machine (Raspberry Pi, server, or your PC) that checks hourly and emails/pushes a notification when the page content changes.
- Example (Python) — run hourly via cron:
  - Script outline:
    - fetch page
    - normalize text (strip scripts/styles)
    - compute hash or compare with previous saved copy
    - if changed, save new content and send notification (SMTP, Slack webhook, Telegram, Pushover)
  - I can provide a ready-to-run script and a sample cron line.

4) GitHub Actions (cloud, free tier)
- Put a small workflow in a repo that runs hourly and uses actions to fetch the page, diff it, and push a notification (email via external service, or Slack webhook).
- Good if you prefer a cloud solution without hosting.

5) Serverless (AWS Lambda / Google Cloud Functions)
- Deploy a function and schedule it (CloudWatch Events / Cloud Scheduler) to run hourly; sends notifications via SNS, Slack, or email.
- Better for production-grade monitoring.

What I can do right now
- Provide a complete, ready-to-run Python script plus instructions to set it up with cron (or systemd timer), including examples for sending email, Slack, or Telegram notifications.
- Or draft the exact steps for a selected web-monitoring service and suggested settings (check frequency, sensitivity, ignore selectors).
- Or prepare a GitHub Actions workflow file you can paste into a repo.

Quick example (Python outline — I will expand if you want):
- Requirements: requests, beautifulsoup4
- Logic:
  1. GET the page URL
  2. Extract main text (BeautifulSoup: remove scripts/styles, get visible text)
  3. Normalize whitespace and compute SHA256 hash
  4. Compare to saved hash in local file
  5. If changed, save new hash and send notification (SMTP example or webhook)

Next steps
- Tell me:
  1. The exact URL of the Acme product-recall page (or paste the HTML/text if it’s private).  
  2. Which notification method you want (email, Slack, SMS, Telegram, Pushover).  
  3. Which option above you prefer (service, browser extension, script+cron, GitHub Actions, serverless).  
  4. Your technical comfort level (I’ll tailor instructions from copy-paste to fully explained).

Once you tell me, I’ll provide the precise script/workflow and setup instructions.
